consensus_summary: Primary consensus meaning of kanaph/wings is divine protective refuge and shelter (bird covering young), with garment-edge/covenant covering, healing, cherubic presence, and swiftness as common secondary senses due to Hebrew polysemy.
book_summary: Wings (kanaph) identified as the covenant edge—wing, skirt, border, corner—where the reminder of the law is bound and refuge is found.
book_core_identification: Covenant edge (wing/skirt/border/corner) binding law-reminder and refuge
boundary_disagreement: Book centers and unifies the garment-edge/covenant + tzitzit-law sense as the definition itself (with refuge attached), whereas consensus treats pure bird-protection imagery as primary and the edge/covenant reading as a distinct common alternative; angelic, geographic, and pure-swiftness cases fall outside the book's framed core.
material_contradiction: None; both affirm covering/refuge via kanaph, but differ on which semantic pole is definitional.
rationale: Minimum cores share the covering/refuge category and the acknowledged dual sense of kanaph, so the book does not replace the referent. It does, however, materially tighten the primary identification to the covenant-edge pole (law bound at the corner + refuge), reclassifying what consensus lists as secondary into the core while de-emphasizing standalone bird, cherub, or extremity uses. This is boundary refinement, not equivalence or contradiction.
strongest_objection: The dominant biblical and Christian-devotional usage remains the bird-protection motif (Pss, Ruth 2:12, Matt 23:37); elevating only the skirt/edge reading risks under-weighting that primary strand.
